title: Sites choose derive-from-primary or propagate-any-edit, with a Story override
description:
As a publication owner, I want to choose whether translations always follow the primary language or whether an edit in any language can update the others, so each site works the way its editors write.

Design: site setting with a per-Story override (no section override until a section needs one). Derive: edits in a localization are local and pin blocks. Propagate: saving a localization asks 'Only this language' or 'All languages' with no default, plus a reason; 'All languages' translates the changed blocks into the primary as a new primary version that goes through review, then derive updates the others. All propagation passes through the primary. Every version records who, when, why and its scope. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450).

Feature: Sync policies

Scenario: Derive from primary keeps localization edits local
  Given a site that derives translations from English
  When an editor changes a Spanish paragraph
  Then the English Story is unchanged
  And the Spanish paragraph is pinned

Scenario: An edit marked for all languages updates the others through the primary
  Given a site that propagates edits
  When an editor saves a Spanish change for all languages with a reason
  Then a new English version with the change awaits English review
  And once it is accepted the Chinese localization is re-translated for that paragraph only

Scenario: An edit marked for this language only stays put
  Given a site that propagates edits
  When an editor saves a Spanish change for this language only
  Then no other language changes and the Spanish paragraph is pinned
